claim: In many parts of the nervous system, signals pass across multiple synaptic relays on their way to a destination.
source: In many parts of the nervous system, signals pass across multiple synaptic relays on their way to a destination, but little is known about how these relays form and the function they serve.
evidence: This is a general statement about nervous system organization that draws from established neuroscience knowledge.

claim: The organization at successive relays in the parasympathetic nervous system strongly resemble each other despite the different embryological origin and physiological properties of the pre- and postsynaptic cells.
source: We found that the organization at successive relays in the parasympathetic nervous system strongly resemble each other despite the different embryological origin and physiological properties of the pre- and postsynaptic cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on the authors' observations and data.

claim: A similar developmental synaptic pruning and elaboration strategy is used at both sites to generate their adult organizations.
source: Additionally, we found a similar developmental synaptic pruning and elaboration strategy is used at both sites to generate their adult organizations.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on developmental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Neural networks undergo synaptic reorganization in early postnatal life that may allow the nervous system to tune itself to the particular environment in which an animal finds itself.
source: In mammals, neural networks undergo synaptic reorganization in early postnatal life that may allow the nervous system to tune itself to the particular environment in which an animal finds itself (see Shatz (1996); Lichtman and Colman (2000) for reviews).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: There are alterations in connectivity throughout the visual pathway between the retina and visual cortex.
source: In the visual system, the evidence suggests that there are alterations in connectivity throughout the visual pathway between the retina and visual cortex (Wang et al., 2001; Chen and Regehr, 2000; Shatz, 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The segregation of ocular dominance columns in layer IV of primary visual cortex is thought to have a parallel in the development of monocular strips in the dLGN nucleus of the thalamus.
source: Notably, the segregation of ocular dominance columns in layer IV of primary visual cortex is thought to have a parallel in the development of monocular strips in the dLGN nucleus of the thalamus.
evidence: This is a statement about established neuroscience knowledge regarding visual system development.

claim: The segregation of left and right eye input may be essential for depth perception via inter-ocular image disparity.
source: This segregation of left and right eye input may be essential for depth perception via inter-ocular image disparity (Barlow et al., 1967).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and involves speculation about functional significance.

claim: Analogous reorganizations occur in non-sensory systems such as the cerebellum, the efferent motor, and autonomic systems.
source: Analogous reorganizations also occur in non-sensory systems such as the cerebellum (Hashimoto and Kano, 2013), the efferent motor, and autonomic systems (Brown et al., 1976; Lichtman, 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The most detailed analysis of developmental reorganization has been undertaken for motor axonal innervation of muscle fibers.
source: Indeed, perhaps the most detailed analysis of developmental reorganization has been undertaken for motor axonal innervation of muscle fibers.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field based on established knowledge.

claim: It remains unclear what purpose synapse elimination serves in efferent systems.
source: It remains unclear, however, what purpose synapse elimination serves in efferent systems.
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The innervation to submandibular ganglion cells undergoes profound reorganization during postnatal development leaving individual ganglion cells in the adult innervated by many-fold fewer axons than they were at birth.
source: It is known from electrophysiological studies done in the last century that the innervation to submandibular ganglion cells undergoes profound reorganization during postnatal development leaving individual ganglion cells in the adult innervated by many-fold fewer axons than they were at birth (Lichtman, 1977, 1980).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to electrophysiological studies.

claim: An adult ganglion cell is innervated by only one axon that has sufficient quantal content to bring it to the threshold.
source: In general, an adult ganglion cell is innervated by only one axon that has sufficient quantal content to bring it to the threshold.
evidence: This is a statement based on established electrophysiological knowledge.

claim: Individual ganglion cells project to a circumscribed region of the gland and all the ganglion cells projecting to the same region appear to be innervated by the same preganglionic axon.
source: Recently using a retrograde labeling technique, we showed that individual ganglion cells project to a circumscribed region of the gland and that all the ganglion cells projecting to the same region appear to be innervated by the same preganglionic axon (Tsuriel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Salivary secretory cells (acinar cells) are arranged much like grapes on a stem and secrete saliva into the lumens of a highly branched ductal network.
source: Histological studies show that salivary secretory cells (acinar cells) are arranged much like grapes on a stem and secrete saliva into the lumens of a highly branched ductal network (intercalated ducts) that converge into progressively larger ducts.
evidence: This is based on histological studies and established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The terminal axonal arbors of adult parasympathetic postganglionic axons show multiple basket-like structures each with dense agglomerations of boutons.
source: The terminal axonal arbors of adult parasympathetic postganglionic axons (from Thy1 CFP-D mouse line), showing multiple basket-like structures (asterisks) each with dense agglomerations of boutons.
evidence: This is directly observed in the data and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Sympathetic postganglionic axons exhibit sparse terminal arbors with multiple varicosities rather homogenously distributed, resulting in a punctate appearance.
source: Sympathetic postganglionic axons (Thy1 YFP16) exhibit sparse terminal arbors with multiple varicosities rather homogenously distributed, resulting in a punctate appearance.
evidence: This is directly observed in the data and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The basket-like terminals arborized at the site of the intercalated duct-acinar cell assemblies.
source: We co-labeled the axons and the parenchyma and found that the basket-like terminals arborized at the site of the intercalated duct-acinar cell assemblies (Figure 2A–C, arrows; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on co-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Parasympathetic innervation is focused on ducts and largely absent from acinar cells.
source: This result implies that parasympathetic innervation is focused on ducts and largely absent from acinar cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that fine terminal ducts extend beyond the axon baskets to acinar cells.

claim: Individual baskets of different parasympathetic axons segregate onto non-overlapping regions.
source: Labeling of four different parasympathetic axonal terminal arbors with different fluorescent colors (using Brainbow AAV injection) shows that individual baskets of different axons segregate onto non-overlapping regions (yellow green, dark orange, orange and green asterisks).
evidence: This is directly observed using Brainbow labeling shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Intercalated duct - acinar cell assemblies are each generally innervated by only one axon.
source: This lack of overlap was despite transfection of >80% of the ganglion cells, arguing that intercalated duct - acinar cell assemblies are each generally innervated by only one axon.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of overlap despite high transfection efficiency.

claim: The salivary gland parenchyma peripheral to the larger striated ducts contains three major cell types: acinar cells, epithelial cells of the intercalated ducts, and myoepithelial cells.
source: As shown in Figure 3 and Video 2, we found that the salivary gland parenchyma peripheral to the larger striated ducts contains three major cell types: (1) acinar cells, which have small eccentric nuclei and cytoplasm filled with extensive endoplasmic reticulum (Terasaki et al., 2013), along with numerous large vacuoles presumably containing saliva (Figure 3A); (2) epithelial cells of the intercalated ducts ('duct cells') that form the lumens that collect salivary secretions from the nearby acinar cells (Figure 3B); and (3) the myoepithelial cells which grow along the surfaces of both acinar and intercalated duct cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on serial section electron microscopy reconstruction shown in Figure 3.

claim: There are electrical junctions between acinar and duct cells and myoepithelial cells.
source: Because there are electrical junctions between acinar and duct cells and myoepithelial cells (Ihara et al., 2000; Kater and Galvin, 1978) it is possible that the intercalated duct - acinar cell assembly operates as a functional unit.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Axons innervated the intercalated duct cells directly but they also innervated adjacent myoepithelial cells and more rarely acinar cells with a ratio of ~25% synapses on duct cells: ~73% on myoepithelial cells: ~2% on acinar cells.
source: The electron microscopy confirmed that axons innervated the intercalated duct cells directly but they also innervated adjacent myoepithelial cells and more rarely acinar cells with a ratio of ~25% synapses (also known as neuroeffector junctions) on duct cells: ~73% on myoepithelial cells: ~2% on acinar cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Only one axon was responsible for making all the synapses in the reconstructed region onto five acinar cells, six duct cells and several myoepithelial cells.
source: Although we saw multiple different axonal processes near these glandular structures, only one axon was responsible for making all the synapses in this region (onto five acinar cells, six duct cells and several myoepithelial cells).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy reconstruction of a specific volume.

claim: The reconstructed axon did not come into close contact with any other axon through most of its terminal course suggesting that local interactions between different postganglionic axons were rare at sites of innervation.
source: Moreover, the reconstructed axon did not come into close contact with any other axon through most of its terminal course suggesting that local interactions between different postganglionic axons were rare at sites of innervation.
evidence: This is based on observation from electron microscopy reconstruction and involves inference about axon interactions.

claim: Each neuron's axon showed a clumpy distribution of terminal branches (i.e. baskets) that were confined to relatively small portions of the gland (all a neuron's branches were within ~1% of the flattened gland area).
source: Each neuron's axon showed a clumpy distribution of terminal branches (i.e. baskets) that were confined to relatively small portions of the gland (all a neuron's branches were within ~1% of the flattened gland area; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on confocal imaging and reconstruction of single axons shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The axons of each of the four ganglion cells elaborated on average 13.75 baskets (14, 14, 12, 15).
source: The axons of each of the four ganglion cells elaborated on average 13.75 baskets (14, 14, 12, 15; Figure 4A asterisks).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of reconstructed axons shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The absolute size of P1 axon arbors was not significantly different from those at P21.
source: The absolute size of P1 axon arbors (Figure 4B) was not significantly different from those at P21 (mean, N = 17, 0.24 ± 0/165/165 mm2 versus 0.29 ± 0.016 mm2, 95% CI = (−0.158, 0.0517), two tail p>0.29, Two-sample T test assuming unequal variances; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of measured axon arbor sizes shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The P1 gland is much smaller than the gland at P21.
source: However, because the P1 gland is much smaller than the gland at P21 (mean, N = 17, 10.814 ± 1.768 mm2 versus 35.24 ± 4.26 mm2 respectively; two tail p<0.001, 95% CI = (8.98, 11.57), Two-sample T test assuming unequal variances; Figure 4D), the neonatal axons occupied a much larger proportion of the gland (mean, N = 17, P1: 1.8% ± 0.012% versus P21: 0.6% ± 0.6%, two tail p=0.005, 95% CI = (0.0043, 0.0197), Two-sample T test assuming unequal variances; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of measured gland sizes shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The neonatal axons occupied a much larger proportion of the gland compared to P21.
source: However, because the P1 gland is much smaller than the gland at P21 (mean, N = 17, 10.814 ± 1.768 mm2 versus 35.24 ± 4.26 mm2 respectively; two tail p<0.001, 95% CI = (8.98, 11.57), Two-sample T test assuming unequal variances; Figure 4D), the neonatal axons occupied a much larger proportion of the gland (mean, N = 17, P1: 1.8% ± 0.012% versus P21: 0.6% ± 0.6%, two tail p=0.005, 95% CI = (0.0043, 0.0197), Two-sample T test assuming unequal variances; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of normalized axon arbor sizes shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The axonal arbors become confined to progressively smaller regions of the gland during the first three weeks.
source: This normalization showed that the axonal arbors become confined to progressively smaller regions of the gland, at least during the first three weeks.
evidence: This is based on analysis of normalized axon arbor sizes over development.

claim: At P1 the axons had relatively unbranched termini and showed few basket-like terminals: 12/13 fluorescently labeled ganglion cell axons lacked any evidence of basket terminals whereas almost the entire arbor contained baskets at P21.
source: At P1 the axons had relatively unbranched termini and showed few basket-like terminals: 12/13 fluorescently labeled ganglion cell axons lacked any evidence of basket terminals whereas almost the entire arbor contained baskets at P21 (compare Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of axon morphology at different ages shown in Figures 4A and B.

claim: There are more non-basket axon terminals at birth than the total number of baskets plus non-basket endings later on.
source: There are more non-basket axon terminals at birth than the total number of baskets plus non-basket endings later on (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: There are three potential fates for the non-basket endings: some transform into baskets, some are pruned, and some are maintained.
source: This result suggests that there are three potential fates for the non-basket endings: some transform into baskets, some are pruned, and some are maintained.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that non-basket terminals decrease while baskets increase during development.

claim: There were more branches of high orders (i.e. distal branches) at P7 than at P1.
source: We found that there were more branches of high orders (i.e. distal branches) at P7 than at P1 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on branch order analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The overlap of axonal arbors in the gland decreased during early postnatal life.
source: Moreover, the overlap of axonal arbors in the gland decreased during early postnatal life (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of arbor overlap shown in Figure 5F.

claim: At P3 boutons of multiple postganglionic axons overlapped extensively in the same regions.
source: At P3 we found that boutons of multiple postganglionic axons overlapped extensively in the same regions (Figure 7B, asterisks).
evidence: This is directly observed using multicolor labeling shown in Figure 7B.

claim: At P7 the baskets showed no intermixing among different parasympathetic axons.
source: At P7 the baskets however, showed no intermixing among different parasympathetic axons (Figure 7F–H).
evidence: This is directly observed using YFP labeling and VAChT immunostaining shown in Figure 7F-H.

claim: Multiple axonal branches come in close contact with an intercalated duct - acinar cell assembly at P3.
source: Consistent with the Brainbow light microscopy results in which multiple different axons arborized within microns of one another (Figure 7B), there were multiple axonal branches coming in close contact with an intercalated duct - acinar cell assembly (Figure 8A, white arrow).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy reconstruction shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Clusters of synaptic vesicles can be seen along the branches of several different axons and these are in close proximity to the duct cells at P3.
source: In addition, clusters of synaptic vesicles can be seen along the branches of several different axons and these are in close proximity to the duct cells (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This is directly observed in electron microscopy images shown in Figure 8B-D.

claim: Non-basket axonal innervation to single intercalated duct – acinar cell assemblies appears to be derived from more than one axon in early postnatal development.
source: Thus, non-basket axonal innervation to single intercalated duct – acinar cell assemblies appears to be derived from more than one axon in early postnatal development.
evidence: This is inferred from the electron microscopy observations of multiple axons with vesicles near the same assembly.

claim: Synapse elimination occurs in the developing submandibular gland ultimately leaving each intercalated duct- acinar cell assembly singly innervated.
source: This result suggests that synapse elimination occurs in the developing submandibular gland ultimately leaving each intercalated duct- acinar cell assembly singly innervated.
evidence: This is inferred from the developmental transition from multiple to single innervation.

claim: Adult submandibular ganglion cells are typically singly innervated by their brainstem input following a period of synapse elimination during development.
source: Previous evidence indicates that adult submandibular ganglion cells are typically singly innervated by their brainstem input following a period of synapse elimination during development (Lichtman, 1977).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous electrophysiological work.

claim: Single preganglionic axons established multiple basket endings, each on a different ganglion cell.
source: We observed that single axons established multiple basket endings, each on a different ganglion cell.
evidence: This is based on reconstruction of individual preganglionic axons.

claim: Rodent submandibular ganglion cells are mostly adendritic in adults.
source: Because rodent submandibular ganglion cells are mostly adendritic in adults, these baskets are therefore the anatomical correlate of the strong dominance of one synaptic input to each ganglion cell (Coggan et al., 2004; Lichtman, 1977; McCann and Lichtman, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Preganglionic axons did not, as a rule, innervate immediately adjacent ganglion cells.
source: Tracing out individual preganglionic axons showed that they did not, as a rule, innervate immediately adjacent ganglion cells.
evidence: This is based on reconstruction of individual preganglionic axons.

claim: The axon shown in Figure 9A elaborated 25 sporadically distributed baskets within two ganglion cell clusters of several hundred cells.
source: For example, the axon shown in Figure 9A elaborated 25 sporadically distributed baskets within two ganglion cell clusters of several hundred cells.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of a reconstructed axon shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Preganglionic axons also possessed a small number of branches that terminated without a basket.
source: In addition to the baskets, preganglionic axons also possessed a small number of branches that terminated without a basket (Figure 9A inset, arrow).
evidence: This is directly observed in reconstructed axons shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Unbranched endings of preganglionic axons may be the anatomical basis for the occasional weak secondary synaptic inputs seen in electrophysiological recordings from submandibular ganglion cells.
source: These unbranched endings may be the anatomical basis for the occasional weak secondary synaptic inputs seen in electrophysiological recordings from submandibular ganglion cells (Lichtman, 1977, 1980; Snider, 1987).
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical observations and supported by citations to electrophysiological studies.

claim: Preganglionic axons at P3 were more highly branched so that preganglionic terminal arbors were in the immediate proximity of a greater number of ganglion cells.
source: First, these axons were more highly branched so that preganglionic terminal arbors were in the immediate proximity of a greater number of ganglion cells (Figure 9B inset).
evidence: This is based on observation of P3 preganglionic axons shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Very few basket-shaped terminal branches were found in P3 preganglionic axons arguing against a dominant axonal driver for each neuron in early postnatal life.
source: Second, we found very few basket-shaped terminal branches arguing against a dominant axonal driver for each neuron in early postnatal life.
evidence: This is based on observation of P3 preganglionic axons and is consistent with electrophysiological data.

claim: Two adjacent ganglion cells at P3 both had multiple dendritic processes unlike ganglion cells at P7 and older.
source: In this dataset, we reconstructed two adjacent ganglion cells. Both neurons had multiple dendritic processes unlike ganglion cells at P7 and older (see Figures 4A and 6B).
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy reconstruction shown in Figure 10.

claim: Two adjacent ganglion cells at P3 were innervated by a large number (14 and 17) of separate axonal branches.
source: In addition, they were innervated by a large number (14 and 17) of separate axonal branches.
evidence: This is based on electron microscopy reconstruction shown in Figure 10.

claim: The vast majority of sampled volumes in P3 preganglionic axons contained only one branch (95.61%, or 9561 out of 10000) and the maximum number of branches was only 2.
source: We found that the vast majority of the sampled volumes contained only one branch (95.61%, or 9561 out of 10000) and the maximum number of branches was only 2 (in 10,000 iterations).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of light microscopy data to estimate branch numbers.

claim: The 14 and 17 branches observed in the P3 ganglion EM dataset most likely represented the actual number of different innervating axons with a lower bound being about half those numbers.
source: Therefore, the 14 and 17 branches we saw most likely represented the actual number of different innervating axons with a lower bound being about half those numbers.
evidence: This is inferred from the computational analysis of branch numbers in sampled volumes.

claim: In both parts of the parasympathetic pathway, target regions are innervated by only one axon.
source: First, in both parts of the pathway, target regions are innervated by only one axon.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: In both parts of the parasympathetic pathway, axons form basket-like endings to encompass the targets they innervate.
source: Second, in both parts of this pathway, axons form basket-like endings to encompass the targets they innervate.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: In both parts of the parasympathetic pathway, the single innervation emerges only after an earlier period when multiple axons co-innervate the same targets.
source: Fourth, in both parts of this pathway, the single innervation emerges only after an earlier period when multiple axons co-innervate the same targets.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the developmental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: In both parts of the parasympathetic pathway, the pruning process that removes this intermixing occurs during early postnatal life.
source: Finally, in both parts of this pathway, the pruning process that removes this intermixing occurs during early postnatal life.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the developmental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The removal of multiple axonal convergence (i.e., synapse elimination) is central to the establishment of the adult organization of both the gland and ganglia regions of the parasympathetic outflow.
source: Given the developmental parallels in gland and ganglia, it is evident that the removal of multiple axonal convergence (i.e., synapse elimination) is central to the establishment of the adult organization of both these regions of the parasympathetic outflow.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the developmental observations.

claim: Axonal reorganization in glands is the second known site (skeletal muscle being the first) where axonal reorganizations are taking place in targets that are non-neuronal.
source: This axonal reorganization in glands is the second known site (skeletal muscle being the first) where axonal reorganizations are taking place in targets that are non-neuronal.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding based on knowledge of the field.

claim: In glands, the target cells do not fire action potentials and use metabotropic muscarinic rather than ionotropic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
source: However, in glands, the target cells do not fire action potentials and use metabotropic muscarinic rather than ionotropic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (Ekstrom et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The only skeletal muscles that ordinarily do not undergo synapse elimination are tonic muscle fibers that do not fire action potentials.
source: This is significant because the only skeletal muscles that ordinarily do not undergo synapse elimination are tonic muscle fibers that do not fire action potentials (Lichtman et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In experiments in which action potentials are blocked at reinnervated twitch neuromuscular junctions, synapse elimination apparently still occurs suggesting that action potential activity may not always be required.
source: However, in experiments in which action potentials are blocked at reinnervated twitch neuromuscular junctions, synapse elimination apparently still occurs suggesting that action potential activity may not always be required (Costanzo et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous experimental work.

claim: Axon pruning in normal development can occur without sodium-based postsynaptic action potential activity.
source: The result described here in salivary glands argues that axon pruning in normal development can occur without sodium-based postsynaptic action potential activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of synapse elimination in glands where target cells don't fire action potentials.

claim: Voltage-dependent calcium channels in postsynaptic targets mediate early stages of synaptic competition among the cerebellar climbing fibers innervating Purkinje cells.
source: It is known that voltage-dependent calcium channels in postsynaptic targets also mediate early stages of synaptic competition among the cerebellar climbing fibers innervating Purkinje cells (Kano et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A neurotransmitter-elicited calcium surge occurs in myoepithelial cells.
source: A neurotransmitter-elicited calcium surge also occurs in myoepithelial cells (Ekstrom et al., 1998) raising the possibility that a calcium flux in the myoepithelial cells could play a critical role in the synaptic modifications in the gland.
evidence: This is supported by a citation and involves speculation about mechanism.

claim: The large number of electrical junctions between myoepithelial cells in glands may allow synchronous calcium waves to pass through the assembly following nerve stimulation and mediate synapse loss to the whole assembly.
source: The large number of electrical junctions between myoepithelial cells in glands (Ihara et al., 2000; Taugner and Schiller, 1980) may allow synchronous calcium waves to pass through the assembly following nerve stimulation and mediate synapse loss to the whole assembly.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism based on known properties of myoepithelial cells.

claim: Individual muscle fibers are electrically disconnected with each other during the phase of synapse elimination, leading to relatively few instances where immediate adjacent muscle fibers are part of the same motor unit.
source: This contrasts with the situation in skeletal muscle where individual muscle fibers are electrically disconnected with each other during the phase of synapse elimination, leading to relatively few instances where immediate adjacent muscle fibers are part of the same motor unit (Keller-Peck et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Each single brainstem axon focuses large numbers of synapses (baskets) onto each of a sporadically distributed cohort of ganglion cells.
source: The axonal expression of fluorescent protein we describe shows that in adult animals each single brainstem axon focuses large numbers of synapses (baskets) onto each of a sporadically distributed cohort of ganglion cells (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is based on the anatomical data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The activity patterns of the cohort of ganglion cells innervated by the same brainstem axon are synchronous with each other.
source: Based on electrophysiology (Coggan et al., 2004; see also Lichtman, 1977) we know these ganglion cells are driven to threshold by only one input (presumably the source of the basket) and therefore we expect that the activity patterns of the cohort innervated by the same brainstem axon are synchronous with each other.
evidence: This is inferred from electrophysiological data cited from previous studies.

claim: Many neighboring baskets despite being innervated by different ganglion cells may be activated at the same time by virtue of the synchronous activity of a cohort of ganglion cells.
source: Therefore, many neighboring baskets despite being innervated by different ganglion cells may nonetheless be activated at the same time by the virtue of the synchronous activity of a cohort of ganglion cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical organization and electrophysiological properties.

claim: One preganglionic axon drives a potentially contiguous territory in the gland.
source: This arrangement would lead to an anatomical unit of secretion wherein one preganglionic axon drives a potentially contiguous territory in the gland.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical organization described.

claim: Activity in one brainstem preganglionic neuron could potentially produce salivary flow that overcomes the compliance of the ductal network and thus reach the oral cavity.
source: Such a 'neuro-lobular' organization might be advantageous because activity in one brainstem preganglionic neuron could potentially produce salivary flow that overcomes the compliance of the ductal network (Ekstrom et al., 1998) and thus reach the oral cavity.
evidence: This is a speculative functional interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: Motor units are often restricted to sub-compartments of a muscle.
source: A similar issue arises in skeletal muscle where motor units (which synchronously drive many muscle fibers) are often restricted to sub-compartments of a muscle (Keen and Fuglevand, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The tension elicited by the simultaneous activation of a number of neighboring muscle fibers is more effective than the same amount of tension if distributed over a larger area because the coordinated local contraction overcomes the visco-elastic properties of muscle and tendon.
source: The tension elicited by the simultaneous activation of a number of neighboring muscle fibers is more effective than the same amount of tension if distributed over a larger area because the coordinated local contraction overcomes the visco-elastic properties of muscle and tendon.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of muscle physiology.

claim: If synapse elimination did not occur in the gland, then each ganglion cell axon would likely retain small connections to many multiply innervated intercalated duct - acinar cell assemblies rather than strong input to a smaller number of postsynaptic targets.
source: If synapse elimination did not occur in the gland, then each ganglion cell axon would likely retain small connections to many multiply innervated intercalated duct - acinar cell assemblies rather than strong input to a smaller number of postsynaptic targets.
evidence: This is a speculative counterfactual reasoning about the consequences of no synapse elimination.

claim: Synapse elimination occurs when the multiple inputs to the same postsynaptic target are asynchronously active.
source: A number of experiments show that synapse elimination occurs when the multiple inputs to the same postsynaptic target are asynchronously active (reviewed in Tapia and Lichtman, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: The reorganization of the wiring of the peripheral part of the pathway (postganglionic input to gland targets) must occur before synapse elimination of the more centrally located preganglionic input to ganglion cells.
source: If synapse elimination in the parasympathetic nervous system is also mediated by asynchronous activity, then the reorganization of the wiring of the peripheral part of the pathway (postganglionic input to gland targets) must occur before synapse elimination of the more centrally located preganglionic input to ganglion cells (Figure 11).
evidence: This is inferred from the logic of activity-dependent synapse elimination and illustrated in Figure 11.

claim: If ganglion cells became singly innervated before the gland targets did, then there would be multiple ganglion cells with identical activity innervating the same gland targets, and because of their synchronous activity synapse elimination would not occur.
source: To make this argument we imagine what would be the consequence had synapse elimination occurred in the opposite order: first in the preganglionics (as opposed to first in the gland). If ganglion cells became singly innervated before the gland targets did, then there would be multiple ganglion cells with identical activity (i.e., all activated by the same preganglionic axon) innervating the same gland targets. Because of their synchronous activity synapse elimination would not occur, resulting in multiply innervated gland targets (Figure 11, left).
evidence: This is a logical argument based on the principles of activity-dependent synapse elimination.

claim: Experiments that synchronize motor axon activity patterns abolish synapse elimination.
source: For example, experiments that synchronize motor axon activity patterns abolish synapse elimination (Favero et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous experimental work.

claim: Basket-like endings are visible in the gland before basket-like endings are visible in the ganglion.
source: Evidence that is consistent with this view includes the following: first, basket-like endings are visible in the gland before basket-like endings are visible in the ganglion (preliminary data);
evidence: This is based on preliminary observations by the authors.

claim: The end of synapse elimination in the ganglia of rodents occurs around 30 days postnatal, which is weeks after the anatomy of the gland stabilizes.

evidence: This is based on the developmental timeline data presented in the manuscript.
